newsitem.title: USA: International Aero wins aircraft engine contract.
newsitem.headline: International Aero wins aircraft engine contract.

text.p: International Aero Engines said Monday it had won a contract from SilkAir that was "potentially worth" $250 million.
The engines will power SilkAir's new fleet of eight firm and 10 option Airbus Industrie A320 family aircraft, International Aero said in a statement.

International Aero is a consortium in which United Technologies Corp unit Pratt & Whitney owns 33 percent; Rolls-Royce Plc owns 33 percent; and Daimler-Benz AG unit MTU owns 12 percent. The balance is owned by Japanese Aero Engines Corp.
Asian regional carrier SilkAir is a subsidiary of Singapore Airlines, and is a new customer for International Aero.
Deliveries of the eight firm aircraft -- a mix of A320s and A319s -- will begin in September 1998, International Aero said.
SilkAir is now the 14th International Aero V2500-powered Airbus Industrie customer in the Asia-Pacific region.
International Aero said it has 69 V2500 customers worldwide and an order book of $13 billion.
